highlights.title: California tightens rules on AI data center energy and water use
highlights.summary: California Gov. Gavin Newsom has signed seven bills designed to prevent AI data centers from passing utility costs onto residents, as reported earlier by the Los Angeles Times.
body: Gavin Newsom signed a package of bills requiring AI data centers to pay for upgrades to the local energy grid.

Other bills included in the package will require proposed data centers to disclose their estimated water use to local governments, along with information about energy efficiency and drought planning. They must also meet certain energy, water, and fuel consumption requirements before qualifying for a streamlined approval process. Last week, Newsom signed an executive order to speed up the creation of an AI “kill switch.”

“While the Trump administration moves toward deregulation, communities are left to deal with the consequences — higher electricity demand, grid constraints, water use, and pollution,” Newsom says in the press release. “With these laws, we are ensuring that Californians remain in the driver’s seat — and that those profiting from data centers aren’t doing so at our expense.”

highlights.title: 'Just getting started' - Pollock signs new multi-year deal with Saints
highlights.summary: Henry Pollock has signed a new multi-year contract extension with Northampton Saints that will see him stay at his boyhood club beyond this season.
body: In a statement, Pollock said: "I'm massively happy to re-sign with Saints, my boyhood club. It's an exciting place to be right now. We're in a great spot as a team, but it feels like there's still so much more growth in us.

"I'm still young, and we've got a young squad with a brilliant group of lads. Some of my best mates are here, and every day everyone pushes each other to improve and be the best players and team we can be. For where I am in my career, this is exactly where I want to be.

"I feel like we're only just getting started. We won the PREM last season and we want to go again. Winning the Champions Cup is another huge ambition for us. We came so close a couple of years ago, and achieving that together would be incredibly special.

"I just want to enjoy every moment of this journey. I'm playing for my boyhood club, surrounded by great people, and that's something I never take for granted. The connections within this group are what make it such a special place."

highlights.title: Second wave of Xbox cuts reported to be happening this week, with "several" studios apparently facing consolidation
highlights.summary: Xbox is reportedly preparing to lay off hundreds more people this week as the company plans to consolidate several of its studios.
body: The news comes from an exclusive report on The Information, which cites a source briefed about Microsoft's plans. The report does not say which of Xbox's many studios are affected and which are being consolidated.

If correct, this would be the second wave of Xbox layoffs this year, following major restructuring in July that resulted in 1,600 job cuts. This is part of Xbox CEO Asha Sharma's plan to "reset" Microsoft's gaming division and return it to profitability. When those cuts were announced, Sharma also said the company intended to cut a further 1,600 jobs before a year had passed (taking us to next summer, approximately). These reported layoffs could be that second wave.

July's layoffs saw cuts across almost the entirety of Xbox's studio portfolio, though some teams were more affected than others. Xbox also shed a handful of studios, with some of those, such as Double Fine Productions and Compulsion Games, buying back their independence. Other studios, such as Ninja Theory and State of Decay maker Undead Labs, were instead sold to as-yet unnamed buyers, and Dishonored studio Arkane Lyon is undergoing consultation, and its fate remains unknown.

highlights.title: Apple Reveals Apple Music Hall, a New Live Venue in London
highlights.summary: Apple is bringing a new live music venue to London. Located in Battersea Power Station, Apple Music Hall is a state-of-the-art venue “designed to connect artists and fans through bespoke, intimate performances unlike anywhere else,” Apple said in its announcement on Tuesday.
body: Apple Music Hall is also an operational production facility, with two recording and mixing studios built to professional standards. The venue is hardwired for 16+ cameras with a broadcast control room that also supports iPhone video capture.

“In short, an artist can perform an intimate live show for fans at Apple Music Hall and walk out with a finished Spatial Audio recording, a broadcast-ready mix, and multicamera video — all from a single show,” a press release states. “Performances out of Apple Music Hall will also be livestreamed globally so fans outside of London can tune in to enjoy these one-time-only shows from their favorite artists.”

“At Apple Music, we care deeply about music, the artists who make it and their life stories,” added Zane Lowe, Apple Music’s global creative director and lead anchor for Apple Music 1. “We’re always looking for new opportunities to connect the artists and the fans because we are fans. What better way to celebrate this relationship than a new music venue where we get to experience amazing music in an amazing space and share it with the world. Great music and memories will be made at Apple Music Hall.”

highlights.title: The pest I’ll never forget: I awoke to the sound of my bedroom bin rustling
highlights.summary: At first the mice were just a distant pitter-patter. But soon they had an unblinking confidence that they owned the entire house and all the food in it. Living in a nine-person house in Vancouver, Canada, far from my UK home, came with plenty of benefits. Cleanliness was not one of them.
body: In the winter of 2023, one of my housemates began to hear the sound of creatures rattling around in the ceiling of her basement room. The pitter-patters grew louder and louder; others began to report sightings from across the house. It wasn’t long before I was waking to the sound of my bedroom bin rustling. I had to accept it: we had mice.

When I saw my first mouse scuttling across the kitchen floor, my body filled with dread at the battle I knew we had ahead. Sleep quickly became a luxury. My housemate claimed she could hear hundreds of mice partying above her head. Frustrated with her inability to sleep, she would regularly hit her ceiling panels and be rewarded by a mouse falling on her face in return.

There was rarely a day when any food left in the cupboard hadn’t been gnawed through. I spent many mornings staring at my sourdough bread and questioning whether the large holes in it were from natural causes or mouse-made. I even began to believe I could recognise the taste of food that had also been sampled by our tiny friends. It all sounds mad, but it became hard to work out what was real or not when every time you walked into a room you were greeted by a squeal.
points: At first the mice were just a distant pitter-patter.
But soon they had an unblinking confidence that they owned the entire house and all the food in it.
In the winter of 2023, one of my housemates began to hear the sound of creatures rattling around in the ceiling of her basement room.
It wasn’t long before I was waking to the sound of my bedroom bin rustling.

highlights.title: AI, Tariffs, Rare Minerals: What to Expect From Trump’s Upcoming Summit With Xi Jinping
highlights.summary: Washington and Beijing have grown ever more linked in the AI boom, making hardware exports and technological restrictions hefty bargaining chips in negotiations.
body: Of all the events in the United Nations General Assembly taking place this week, the most anticipated by far is the upcoming meeting between Donald Trump and Chinese president Xi Jinping.

Though the majority of the diplomatic activities are happening in New York, this face-to-face between the two leaders will take place at the White House. Trump is scheduled to personally welcome Xi at Joint Base Andrews on Wednesday, September 23—an unusual diplomatic gesture, as US presidents do not typically go to the airport to welcome foreign leaders.

Ahead of that airport reunion, a US delegation led by Treasury secretary Scott Bessent and trade representative Jamieson Greer is meeting with He Lifeng, China’s vice premier of the State Council, to set the agenda. The World Economic Forum presented an overview of some of the most pressing topics, including the trade conflict, the supply chain, technological competition, and the ever-sensitive issue of Taiwan—all while keeping in mind the difficulties that have kept the US mired in a war in the Middle East that threatens to escalate.

highlights.title: British Columbia sues OpenAI and Sam Altman over Tumbler Ridge mass school shooting
highlights.summary: Canadian province alleges deadly attack could have been prevented if company had warned police of shooter’s ChatGPT use. British Columbia has sued OpenAI in California, saying a mass shooting at a school in the province could have been prevented if the company had warned local ⁠law enforcement that…
body: The lawsuit filed in San Francisco federal court on Monday names OpenAI and its CEO, Sam Altman, as defendants. It is seeking damages to fund recovery efforts in the province after the February attack, as well as an order directing changes to the way the company handles ChatGPT conversations that could lead to violence.

Nine people, primarily children, were killed in the school shooting in Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia. The shooter, Jesse Van ⁠Rootselaar, had been flagged by the company’s safety team after her conversations about gun violence, but the company did not alert police.

Altman published a letter ​to the community saying he was “deeply sorry” OpenAI had not contacted ‌law enforcement. He promised reforms, but never ‌followed through, despite efforts from British Columbia’s attorney general to engage, the lawsuit says.

The school where the shooting took place is in the process of being ‌demolished, and the province has been forced to absorb the costs of a replacement school, mental health care and other effects of the shooting, according to the lawsuit.

body: The Ryder Cup and Solheim Cup both see the best from Europe take on the United States, while the Presidents Cup - live this week on Sky Sports - is a biennial contest between Team USA and an International Team.

The Grant Thornton Invitational is a mixed team tournament taking place every December containing PGA Tour and DP World Tour players, following on from the defunct JCPenney Classic, but is there space for one on an international scale?

A mixed team golf event will feature in the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028, while Team Europe captain Luke Donald recently suggested launching a mixed team event that would share similarities with the Ryder Cup and Solheim Cup.
"I'm all for having some events where we're playing together and sharing each other's talents," Donald told the Telegraph ahead of the BMW PGA Championship. "I think it's great to see that.

highlights.title: 23 Years Later, the Most Addictive Sci-Fi Show Ever Made Officially Blasts Onto Free Streaming
highlights.summary: The show is Battlestar Galactica, Ronald D. Moore’s beloved sci-fi series that ran for four seasons from 2004 to 2009. Once Fred and Carrie start watching, they cannot stop.
body: There’s a classic Portlandia sketch where Fred and Carrie are getting ready to head to a friend’s birthday party, but Fred says they should try out a TV show he’s heard great things about. Carrie reluctantly agrees to try one episode before they leave, but then they have to go to the party. They’ll at least make it there for dessert, right? They do not.

More than two decades after Battlestar Galactica premiered, the show remains dangerously well-engineered for exactly this kind of behavior. And with the entire series streaming for free on Pluto TV, it's remarkably easy for anyone to become Fred and Carrie, or Corey and Kevin.

Battlestar Galactica radically reimagines the campy 1978 series of the same name. Humanity has created a race of artificial beings called Cylons, the robots have rebelled, and they've returned after decades of peace to wipe out the human race. A tiny fleet of survivors escapes under the protection of the aging Battlestar Galactica, led by Commander William Adama (Edward James Olmos), and sets off in search of the mythical planet Earth.
But Battlestar Galactica immediately reveals its best gimmick: Some Cylons look exactly like humans.

highlights.title: ‘To sleep in a sculpture is a wonderful idea’: a hike along Andy Goldsworthy’s epic art trail in Haute-Provence
highlights.summary: A long-distance walking route in the south of France devised by the celebrated land artist offers intrepid hikers an opportunity to immerse themselves in nature and art. At 69, I had never hiked with a backpack and I had no idea what land art was.
body: First, I watch Rivers and Tides, a documentary on Goldsworthy’s work, and discover he has built exquisite ice sculptures and stone cairns in my own country, Canada. His work seems to speak to an older part of the soul. Then, I start walking up hills, gradually adding weights to my backpack until I can comfortably carry 9kg (20lb).

We meet in Digne-les-Bains, a bustling mountain town in the centre of the Unesco geopark of Haute-Provence, and the starting point for a 10-day, 150km (93-mile) hiking route that includes the possibility of staying overnight at seven reservable but free off-grid sleeping cabins. Goldsworthy worked alongside local teams to restore the abandoned shepherd huts, farmhouses, chapel and stone shelters, and created a site-specific artwork for each one. Over four days, we will visit three of these refuges and hike about 45km (28 miles).

highlights.title: Can John Ternus find Apple’s next big thing?
highlights.summary: Today, I’m talking with Mark Gurman, who is the world’s best-sourced Apple reporter — both as Bloomberg’s chief Apple correspondent and the host of the upcoming podcast Power On.
body: Bloomberg’s chief Apple correspondent Mark Gurman on Siri, Tim Cook’s legacy, and what to expect from new CEO John Ternus.
Earlier this month, Apple hosted its annual iPhone hardware event, virtually every detail of which was reported ahead of time by Mark. But this event was special, for a number of reasons.

It was new Apple CEO John Ternus’ first major product launch since he took over for former CEO Tim Cook less than two weeks prior. It was also the debut of the iPhone Duo, Apple’s first foldable smartphone. The timing of those two things was not at all coincidental, as you’ll hear Mark explain. Apple takes these hardware events — and the stories they tell — extremely seriously.

This year’s story actually says a great deal about what’s happening at Apple, how Cook managed in wholesale leadership ranks over the past year, and how all of that might change Apple’s culture. Furthermore, what all that tells about Ternus’ plan to navigate Apple from what you might call the iPhone era into the AI era.

highlights.title: The rise of Big Toothbrush: how did our mouths become such a lucrative market?
highlights.summary: People in the UK are more interested in oral health than ever - and you can now buy prebiotic toothpastes and brushes that cost up to £600. Yet we remain in the midst of a serious dental crisis. A December 1969 report from the consumer magazine Which?
body: In the UK, 59% of adults use an electric toothbrush and sales, including replacement heads, reached £361m in the last year, according to market intelligence company Mintel. Any product launch by Dyson – still associated with reinventing the vacuum cleaner – feels like something of an event, so its incursion into oral health does feel significant, says Rachel Bairsto, the head of museum services at the British Dental Association. “We’re seeing more and more expensive toothbrushes,” she says. “Expensive toothpaste as well.”

These highly designed everyday objects have become symbols of affluence. “If you see a picture of a swanky bathroom, it will definitely have plug sockets for some kind of rechargeable electric toothbrush,” says Bairsto. “Whereas I’ve tried to look through the archives to find pictures of bathrooms with toothbrushes in them, and I can’t. Was everybody appalled at the sight of a toothbrush in the bathroom? I don’t know.” With many toothbrushes now, she says, “I think there’s definitely a status symbol [aspect] to it.”

highlights.title: Injustice 3 Leak Reportedly Reveals 2 Playable Characters
highlights.summary: Injustice 3 will feature one character fans will expect and one who perhaps comes as a surprise, according to a fresh leak. MP1st unearthed evidence to suggest the unannounced fighting game will feature both Supergirl and Batwoman on its roster of playable characters.
body: Batwoman (Kate Kane) dies in the canon Injustice comics, which suggests someone else has taken up the Batwoman mantle for Injustice 3, Kate Kane didn’t actually die, or the game retcons the events of the book. Either way, this is a superhero story we’re talking about — no-one stays dead forever.

Or, as MP1st suggests, Injustice 3 may not continue the story told in Injustice and Injustice 2, but act as a reboot that tells an entirely different story. NetherRealm’s other fighting game franchise, Mortal Kombat, has done this multiple times, so it wouldn’t be a huge surprise with Injustice since it’s been nearly a decade since Injustice 2 came out.

Publisher Warner Bros. has yet to announce another Injustice game, despite it being an open secret at this point. Given Paramount looks like it’s finally going to get the green light to complete its $110 billion merger with Warner Bros., perhaps that will provide some clarity on the company’s video game plan, which we know also include Hogwarts Legacy 2 and a new Batman game from Arkham developer Rocksteady.

highlights.summary: Susan Sarandon will be honored by the Rome Film Festival’s independently run Alice in the City sidebar, which is dedicated to films for children and youth. Sarandon will be attending the Eternal City fest to promote the international launch of “Silicon Valley” star Zach Woods’ feature film debut…
body: Susan Sarandon will be honored by the Rome Film Festival ’s independently run Alice in the City sidebar, which is dedicated to films for children and youth.

“From ‘The Rocky Horror Picture Show’ to ‘The Hunger,’ from ‘The Witches of Eastwick’ to ‘Thelma & Louise,’ to ‘Dead Man Walking,’ Sarandon has spanned decades of cinema, building a gallery of female characters that cannot be reduced to a single model,” the fest said in a statement praising her career. The statement added that the characters she plays in these films are all “Women who question identity, desire, power, rules and freedom.” “But the common thread running through her journey is not only the roles she has chosen,” it continued.

“It is also her ability to maintain her own autonomy from the Hollywood system, bringing together artistic choices, personal freedom and consistency of her own convictions,” the statement went on to point out.

Sarandon, who recently attended the Venice Film Festival in September with her latest film, Italian director Andrea Pallaoro’s “The Echo Chamber,” said in Venice that she continues to be shunned by Hollywood over her outspoken support of Palestine.

highlights.title: My son has left home – and I feel full of complicated joy | Zoe Williams
highlights.summary: I took him to university this weekend, and it reminded me of the exhilaration of suddenly having your own space, absolutely separate from your mother. When kids are small, and their expectations of an event diverge from yours in some important way, you feel terrible about it.
body: Then when they’re “adults”, your expectations diverge again. They thought you’d drop them at university and immediately leave, while you thought you’d unpack, and meet their flatmates, explore the city, and spin round a supermarket, then have a Nando’s, and maybe read a bedtime story, get chatting to the other parents and maybe all do karaoke? Well, then it’s time to manage your own disappointment, and the only thing to be said for that is that it’s way less bad than managing theirs.

When I went to university, my mum’s boyfriend drove me and there wasn’t room for her in the car, so it was a beautifully symmetrical event: I wanted him to leave and he wanted to leave. Then when she came to see me, I would count down the hours until she had to leave, and I used to love it when other people’s mums came to see them, because often they were nice, but, also, the schadenfreude was intense.

highlights.summary: Anya Taylor-Joy has firmly established herself as one of her generation’s leading and most versatile actors. At 30, she has built a career across film and television, appearing in franchises like Super Mario and Mad Max, and winning a Golden Globe for her role in The Queen’s Gambit.
body: The Witch premiered in 2015, serving as a calling card for Taylor-Joy as a rising star and Robert Eggers as a director to look out for. It also turned Black Phillip the goat into a contemporary horror icon almost overnight. More than a decade later, the film remains just as invigorating. It’s currently streaming on Netflix, but only until Oct. 1 — so you’ve got a matter of days left to watch it.

The Witch follows a devout, isolated Puritan family in 1630s New England, a time when witches, myth, and folklore quietly stood at the root of most people’s everyday fears. Following their exile from the religious community due to a dispute with the church, a family of seven is forced to relocate to the outskirts of society, with the dark, unmapped woods mere feet away.

The film is steeped in its historical setting, and its characters speak a dense form of archaic English, with religion at the very center of their lives. That can be a tough watch for modern viewers, but The Witch ultimately tells a simple story about a family hitting its breaking point.

highlights.title: The truth about Sean Combs: ‘No is not a stopping point for him’
highlights.summary: Cheyenne Roundtree, an investigative reporter at Rolling Stone, was as shocked as anyone when allegations of rape and sexual abuse were made against the music mogul. Then she began digging into his past life.
body: For Cheyenne Roundtree, an investigative reporter at Rolling Stone, the civil lawsuit that dropped on Sean “Diddy” Combs in November 2023 seemed to come from nowhere. Filed by his ex-partner, the singer Cassie Ventura, it alleged that Combs had beaten and raped her, plied her with drugs and forced her into sexual encounters with male sex workers throughout their decade-long relationship.

Roundtree, along with much of the world’s media, was shocked. “I’d grown up in the era of Diddy and Cassie and viewed them as this power couple,” she says. “Her hit Me & U was my song. Diddy was this mogul – I knew him for the music – and she was this style inspiration, this beautiful, talented woman living an amazing life.”

“His attorneys took it head on,” says Roundtree. “They were saying: ‘We’re going to own the domestic violence, but that happened in the past – all that is locked in the 2010s and he has changed. He has become Love since then. [Combs had declared in November 2017 that he was renaming himself Love, or Brother Love.] He’s a new person, a father figure.’ But all these other lawsuits were telling a completely different story.”

Ron Johnson, 66, has heard predictions about the demise of physical retail before. “AI is a new technology that will improve the online shopping experience,” Johnson said in an interview. “But I don’t know that it’s going to change which way we shop.”

highlights.title: Black Tesla employees accuse company of fostering racial discrimination in major trial
highlights.summary: Lawyers say Black employees at Tesla experienced ‘rampant racism’ that was left unchecked for years at their flagship factory in California. Dozens of Black employees at Tesla’s flagship plant in California said they were subject to racist slurs, unequal pay and promotions, and bullying by…
body: Their complaints form the basis of a lawsuit brought against the Elon Musk-owned electric car company by the state of California, which began trial with opening statements on Monday.

Brett Watson, a lawyer for the California Civil Rights Department, started by showing the court a series of photographs taken throughout Tesla’s Fremont factory. There was the N-word scratched on to a grey-blue metal surface and written in black marker on a wall. “KKK”, swastikas, the Confederate flag, a white supremacist logo and “go back to Africa” had also been found scrawled in bathrooms, lockers, workplace benches and lunch tables, according to court documents.
Watson listed a long string of racial epithets workers said were directed personally at them, including one incident where a Black worker said he was asked: “You want to hang from a tree?”

“Despite what Tesla might argue, you will hear Black workers were deeply offended,” Watson said. “These experiences cannot be dismissed as a few bad apples … hundreds of complaints to Tesla and [the Civil Rights Department] will show these experiences were not isolated.”

body: One of King's most prophetic books was released in 1982 under the pen name Richard Bachman. The Running Man has a Simpsons -esque knack for predicting our future: a world where spectacle is wielded to influence the public and keep them in line.

While Edgar Wright put a modern spin on King's story in 2025, there's still something charming and surprisingly resonant in the extremely campy version that came out in 1987 starring Arnold Schwarzenegger at the height of his action-star powers. That version of The Running Man is now free to stream on YouTube, and it takes the real and somber concerns of King’s novel to hilarious (and believable) extremes.

Directed by Paul Michael Glaser, The Running Man opens with a helpful crawl in bright white letters over a red backdrop, laying out the vision of the future while establishing the film’s striking color palette.

body: Fariba Hashimi, who is based in Italy, powered home second in the women’s road race near Nagoya in Japan, calling the triumph “something special”.

“I can’t explain my feelings now,” said the 23-year-old, before reflecting on how she was attacked with stones and trained disguised as a man when she started out in the sport as a teenager along with sister Yulduz, who is also now a pro cyclist. “I was born inside a country where the women who dream are getting attacked, and I’m really happy that I have fought against that,” she said. “I hope that the next generation will come here and represent their country without any fear.”
The Taliban authorities returned to power in 2021 and have since imposed a series of rules limiting women’s access to education and public life, including sport.

highlights.title: Amazon wants to help the Colorado River, but we still don’t know how much water the company uses
highlights.summary: Amazon plans to spend $20 million on water conservation projects along the Colorado River, a crucial but dwindling water supply for 40 million people in the Western US. The initiative comes as Amazon and other tech companies face mounting scrutiny over how much water their data centers use.
body: The Colorado River faces an ‘unprecedented’ drought as data centers demand more water.

Amazon announced the launch of a Colorado River Basin Collaborative today, with a mission to “create one of the biggest corporate water conservation efforts for a single U.S. watershed.” It expects to raise $100 million over two years — including the $20 million investment from its own coffers — for water conservation efforts.

Stretching 1,400 miles, the Colorado River brings water to 40 million people across seven states in the Western US and and two states in Mexico. The waterway has faced “unprecedented” drought over the last 26 years, according to the US Bureau of Reclamation. Decades of overuse on top of human-caused climate change have exacerbated the problem. To cope, the US Department of the Interior finalized a plan in August imposing steep water cuts on Arizona, Nevada, and California.

highlights.title: Got an Android Phone? Google Thinks You’ll Probably Want a Googlebook Laptop
highlights.summary: Apple lovers have long enjoyed seamless connectivity between their iPhones and Macs. Now, Google’s bringing that experience to Android.
body: iPhones and Macs are like two peas in a pod. Apple’s hardware synergy means you can launch iPhone apps right from the macOS desktop, respond to texts without picking up your iPhone, and even copy text on one platform and paste it on the other. That kind of seamless connectivity does not natively exist for Android phone owners at the operating system level.

Google’s trying to change that with Googlebooks, a new class of laptop. First teased in May, the company finally shared more details about the new OS at a media-only event in New York City last week. Like with Android, hardware manufacturers can make their own Googlebooks, provided they hit specific standards set by Google.

Today marks the launch of five new computers that comply with the Googlebooks standard, one each from HP, Dell, Lenovo, Acer, and Asus. These machines are powered by either Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X Elite chip or Intel’s Core Ultra 3 (MediaTek also supports the Googlebook platform with its new Dimensity CX C10 Max chip, but none of the new laptops use the chip yet).

body: Just 18 months ago a 31-year-old John Egan was struggling for minutes off the bench for promotion-chasing Burnley and decided to make a January switch to fellow Championship side Hull City.
Fast forward to the present day and Egan is a Premier League regular for the Tigers, who have taken everyone by surprise upon their return to the top flight.

It's been quite a turnaround for the now 33-year-old, who probably thought his last Premier League appearance had already come, when he was taken off on a stretcher with a season-ending Achilles injury when playing for Sheffield United against West Ham in September 2023.
Egan has quietly rebuilt his career after being released by the Blades, first with the Clarets before finding a home at Hull after joining in 2024.

body: Thiruvothu, whose credits include “Bangalore Days,” “Take Off,” “Uyare” and “Virus,” has built a two-decade career largely on roles that push against the structures around her characters.

In “Pradhama Drishtiya Kuttakkar,” produced by Arjun Selva under 11 Icons Film Productions, Thiruvothu plays Aleena Abraham, a woman who becomes a police officer through a compassionate appointment after the death of her husband, also a constable. Set largely inside a local police station, the film follows Aleena alongside fellow officers Divya, Dasan and Sreenath as an unexpected criminal case upends the precinct, testing perceptions of guilt, duty and systemic justice. The film’s plot repeatedly asks how quickly an audience decides someone’s guilt based on incomplete evidence.

Thiruvothu says the film departs from convention by revealing the central crime within its first 10 to 15 minutes, shifting the tension from whodunit to whether the officers involved will be found out.

highlights.summary: Sportswear, showrooms, and supporting domestic talent are on the agenda for this Shanghai Fashion Week season.
body: Shanghai Fashion Week (SHFW) is betting on a more connected fashion ecosystem as it unveils its Spring/Summer 2027 schedule. The upcoming edition, running from October 8-16, will feature more than 80 runway shows and presentations across the city.

The designer schedule remains anchored by Shanghai’s independent fashion scene. Chinese designer brand Hemu will open the week on October 8, marking its 15th SHFW appearance. Established names including Xiaoli, Staffonly, Comme Moi, Shuting Qiu and Short Sentence will return, alongside a younger generation of independent labels.

The underlying message from organizers is straightforward: “local is international”. For this edition, that increasingly means combining Chinese creative talent and global fashion businesses in the same commercial ecosystem, rather than measuring success by the number of foreign names on the calendar.

videos.title: The Steam Frame Shouldn't Work - Here's Why It Does
videos.summary: Lock your cloud storage before AI can scrape it. Get started now with Proton Drive at no cost:
body: Valve's Steam Frame promises your entire Steam library on a standalone headset - but every one of those games was built for x86 processors, and the Frame runs an ARM chip straight out of a smartphone. The trick that makes it possible is FEX, a translator Valve has quietly funded for years that recompiles your games live, while you play. We break down how it works, what it costs in performance, and why it matters way beyond VR with Pierre-Loup Griffais, one of the Valve engineers behind SteamOS.
